profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a mid-sized asset management firm about how to turn a new quant research result on mutual strategy influence among investors into an internal business initiative called the Influence-Aware Allocation Engine. The context is that the firm wants to package the research into something usable for its institutional advisory business before annual client reviews begin in Q4. The agenda is to decide what the pilot will consist of, which client segment it will cover, what data the team will use for calibration and examples, what "validated" means before review, who owns each workstream, and the timeline for an investment committee checkpoint. The expected outcome is an agreed plan for a Q3 pilot, a target audience list, a validation path, and a draft schedule leading to committee review and Q4 rollout activity.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Portfolio optimization, stochastic control, market microstructure, research prototyping
members.background: Elena leads the firm's quantitative research team and previously worked on buy-side portfolio construction models after completing a PhD in applied mathematics focused on dynamic games and control.
members.private_state: She wants to demonstrate that the mutual-influence model is rigorous and practically useful, but she is wary of exposing an early-stage method to clients before the approximation algorithm is stress-tested and stable across edge cases.
hidden_assumptions: A "pilot" for a new allocation model normally means a shadow-mode internal run that compares recommendations against existing portfolios without sending recommendations to clients.
The natural holdings input for model calibration is the month-end custodial snapshot because that is the cleanest, audit-friendly representation of actual positions.
A model is "validated" once the theoretical properties are numerically reproduced, the approximation solver behaves stably, and historical replay results look directionally sensible.
When business colleagues say the "top 20 accounts," they usually mean the largest currently funded institutional mandates by assets under management.
Materials prepared for the investment committee are primarily technical review documents unless someone explicitly asks for a client-facing version.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: Institutional product planning, client segmentation, distribution strategy, internal launch coordination
members.background: Daniel came from an investment consulting firm and now translates research capabilities into offerings for pension, endowment, and outsourced CIO relationships.
members.private_state: He needs a credible new story for relationship managers before Q4 review season and wants the initiative to generate visible client engagement, but he does not want to burden the meeting with what feel like obvious operational details.
hidden_assumptions: A "pilot" means a limited external beta with a few selected relationships receiving model-informed discussion materials, even if the firm does not fully automate trades.
The relevant holdings source is the same positions file used in monthly client reporting, based on the operations feed the relationship teams already recognize.
Something is "validated" when it has benchmark comparisons, understandable examples on flagship mandates, and enough documentation to clear internal product and compliance review.
The "top 20 accounts" refers to the firm's most commercially important relationships, including multi-mandate clients and near-term pipeline prospects, not just current AUM leaders.
Anything going to the investment committee should be close to reusable in a client or sales context unless clearly designated as research-only.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to run a "pilot" in Q3.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means an internal shadow deployment: run the model on selected portfolios, compare outputs offline, and review internally before any client exposure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means a limited external beta: prepare recommendations or discussion memos for selected relationships so client teams can start using the concept in Q4 conversations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In business settings, "pilot" routinely covers both internal shadow tests and limited market-facing trials, so each hears a familiar term and assumes the other is using the same standard meaning.

misalignment_points.topic: Which holdings file is the June baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they will use the "June holdings file" or "June book" for calibration and examples.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the June 30 custodial end-of-month snapshot used by quant and risk teams to anchor actual portfolio states.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the June client-reporting positions feed, which reflects the operations-managed file relationship managers see in monthly packets and may smooth or aggregate exposures differently.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both files are informally called the June book inside the firm, and neither person expects the distinction to matter enough to mention during a planning conversation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the model should be "validated" before committee review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the approximation algorithm reproduces the theoretical convergence behavior, remains numerically stable in stress windows, and generates coherent backtest patterns.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the model has benchmark comparisons on a few recognizable mandates, a plain-language explanation, and enough review materials to pass product and compliance scrutiny.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards sound professionally reasonable and compatible on the surface, so the word "validated" creates false consensus even though they imply different work left to do.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to focus the pilot on the firm's "top 20 accounts."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes this means the 20 largest currently funded institutional mandates by AUM, because those provide clean portfolio data for model runs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes this means the 20 most strategically important relationships, including parent organizations with multiple mandates and a few near-close prospects that sales wants to prioritize.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a settled segmentation label, and each person's interpretation fits normal firm language, so neither hears a reason to restate the inclusion boundary.

If we can lock a sensible timeline before committee season, I can protect the research from being pushed out too early.
